newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese deputies appeal against election delay.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese deputies appeal against election delay.

text.p: Lebanese opposition deputies called on the country's highest court on Wednesday to scrap a law which postponed local elections for a second time.
In an appeal to the Constitutional Council, 14 deputies called on the court to declare the law unconstitutional and cancel it.

The parliament voted last July to delay the municipal council and mayoral elections which were scheduled for June until April 1999 in a move that analysts said was largely due to fears among top political leaders that the results could undermine their power bases.
Parliament had voted last April to delay local polls until April 1998 after Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri said he could not guarantee that a new election law would be ready for next spring.
The delay of elections means Lebanon's municipal councils will be 36-years-old before they are finally renewed. The last local elections took place in 1963.
Most municipalities will be run by government appointees until the elections take place.
The Constitutional Council, the highest court in Lebanon, will have a period of two months to announce its decision on the deputies' appeal. Its ruling is not subject to appeal.
